tools.name: scan_page
tools.description: Scan one public web page for SEO and AI visibility. Returns a 0-100 score, the issues to fix first with why and how, AI readiness, and the key facts (title, description, headings, words, speed, structured data). Use this first for any question about how a page performs in Google or AI search.

tools.name: check_ai_visibility
tools.description: Check whether ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity, Gemini and other AI crawlers may read a page (robots.txt per bot), whether llms.txt exists, how ready the content is for AI answers (11 checks), and how an AI model sees the page as plain text. Use this for questions like 'why does ChatGPT not mention my si

tools.name: check_focus_keyword
tools.description: Check how well a page targets one search term: title, meta description, H1, URL, first 100 words, subheadings, image alt texts and keyword density (flags stuffing over 3%). Returns 8 checks with a tip each.

tools.name: get_fix_pack
tools.description: Generate ready-to-paste HTML for the issues on a page, built from the page's own content: a title tag, meta description, canonical, social (Open Graph) tags, viewport and a JSON-LD starting point. Only issues the page actually has are included.

tools.name: scan_html
tools.description: Scan raw HTML that is not published yet, for example a local build, a template or a draft from your editor. Returns the same score, fixes and AI readiness as scan_page. Pass the full HTML document; url is optional and only used to resolve relative links. Use this in coding assistants to check SEO be

tools.name: rescan_and_compare
tools.description: Scan a live page again and compare it with the previous scan of that page: score change, issues fixed, new issues and AI readiness change. Use this after deploying fixes to confirm they worked, or to catch regressions such as a robots.txt change that suddenly blocks AI crawlers. Repeat until the sco

tools.name: check_snippet
tools.description: Estimate how a title and meta description show in Google: pixel width against the cut-off on desktop and mobile, and the truncated text a searcher would see. No network call. Use it to iterate on title and description variants until they fit.

tools.name: generate_schema
tools.description: Generate a JSON-LD block for a page from its own content and validate it against Google's rich result rules. Types: Article, Product, FAQPage (built from question headings and their answers), Organization (with sameAs links found on the page), BreadcrumbList (from the URL), or auto to pick the best

tools.name: find_answer_passages
tools.description: Find the passages on a page that best answer a given question, the way AI answer engines pick text to quote. Returns the top passages with their heading, word count and whether they are a quotable length (40 to 90 words). Use the result to judge whether the page answers the question well, and to rew

tools.name: generate_llms_txt
tools.description: Build a ready-to-upload llms.txt for a site from its sitemap and home page: site name, summary and the main pages grouped by section. Upload the result to the root of the site, for example https://example.com/llms.txt.

tools.name: ai_crawler_policy
tools.description: Write robots.txt rules for AI crawlers based on a policy, and merge them into the site's current robots.txt. Policies: allow_all, search_only (allow AI search and user-requested fetches, block model training), block_training (same as search_only), block_all. Returns the full new robots.txt and what

tools.name: deep_audit
tools.description: Everything OnPage.dev measures on a page, by section: speed hints from the HTML, links and anchor texts, accessibility basics, image SEO, rich results, security headers, content (words, headings, readability, keywords) and technical facts (status, canonical, robots, redirects, hreflang). Pick sectio

tools.name: check_urls
tools.description: Check up to 20 URLs at once: final status code, the full redirect chain and where each one ends up. Built for site migrations, broken link sweeps and launch checks, for example 'do all old URLs 301 to the right new page?'. Pass expected targets to verify each redirect.

tools.name: test_robots
tools.description: Test a URL against the site's live robots.txt for one or more crawlers, using Google's matching rules (most specific user-agent group, longest matching rule, Allow wins ties, * and $ wildcards). Returns allowed or blocked per crawler and the exact rule that decides it. Optionally test a proposed rob

tools.name: validate_schema
tools.description: Validate JSON-LD you wrote before you publish it: JSON syntax, @context and @type, absolute URLs, ISO dates, and Google's required and recommended fields per rich result type. Accepts a JSON-LD object, an array, a @graph, or a full <script type="application/ld+json"> block.

tools.name: compare_html
tools.description: Compare two versions of a page's HTML, for example before and after a code change, and report what got better or worse for SEO: score, issues fixed and introduced (with stable codes), and changes to title, description, H1, canonical, robots, structured data and word count. Use it in code review to c

tools.name: start_site_audit
tools.description: Start an SEO audit of a whole site (up to 25 pages from the sitemap, or from the home page links when there is no sitemap). Returns an audit_id and the first progress. Then call get_site_audit with that id until status is complete; each call scans the next few pages. The finished audit gives the iss

tools.name: get_site_audit
tools.description: Continue a site audit started with start_site_audit: each call scans the next pages and reports progress. Keep calling until status is complete, then you get the site-wide results. Audits are kept for one hour.

tools.name: suggest_internal_links
tools.description: Suggest which existing pages should link to a target page, with anchor text, based on a completed site audit. tools.name: compare_pages
tools.description: Compare a page with up to 3 competitor pages that rank for the same search: score, AI readiness, words, headings, rich results, speed and more side by side, plus per competitor the issues to fix to catch up, structured data they have, words they use that the page does not (content gaps), and where t

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: scan_page, check_focus_keyword, get_fix_pack, scan_html, generate_schema, check_urls, compare_pages · Private data: scan_html · Public sink: generate_llms_txt, validate_schema.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: scan_page, check_focus_keyword, get_fix_pack, scan_html, generate_schema, check_urls, compare_pages · Private data: scan_html · Public sink: generate_llms_txt, validate_schema

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
